subject: ServiceGuard renewal — priority path & latency uplift
messages:
From: Aaron Gupta <aaron.gupta@nimbus.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal coming up — SLA uplift request

Hi Soojin,

Our renewal for ServiceGuard is up at the end of November (account HS-4982). Usage has grown ~3x in the last 9 months and we're seeing occasional tail latency spikes during peak processing windows. Before we lock term lengths and spend, my leadership is asking if we can: 

- Add a latency SLO (95th percentile) for API responses with a target of <= 200ms for the majority of our traffic.
- Move to a "priority" support path during business hours (US) with a 1-hour response SLA for Sev-1s.
- Reserve a modest capacity bump (20% headroom) for seasonal spikes.

Can you send over a proposal with the SLO language and an idea of uplift pricing / credits for multi-year? Attaching our last 30-day token volume export for context.

Thanks,
Aaron
VP Product, Nimbus Analytics
[Attachment: nimbus-30d-usage.csv (67KB)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Gupta <aaron.gupta@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — SLA uplift request

Hi Aaron —

Thanks for the heads up and the usage export. Congrats on the growth — this is exactly the sort of scale our Dedicated/Reserved playbooks are built for.

I'll pull together a short SLO addendum and a pricing uplift estimate based on the 20% buffer you mentioned. Looping in Ben (account lead) and Marissa (CS) to align on operational handoff and onboarding credits.

Quick questions so we size the proposal correctly:
- Is the 200ms 95th target expected across all model endpoints or only low-latency text-gen routes?
- Any preferred outage or maintenance blackout windows?

I'll aim to get a draft to you by next Monday.

—Soji n
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 10:32:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Nimbus — capacity and SLO feasibility

Team —

Following Aaron's ask (copied below), we need engineering input on what a practical 95th=200ms SLO looks like for their mix. Key constraints: model family is a mix of open Llama variants and a tuned decoder stack; peak concurrency aligns with ETL windows (approx 600-800 concurrent tokens).

Can Ops confirm whether a 20% reserved headroom is feasible in Dedicated (we may suggest burst capacity vs reserved GPUs)? Also want a quick cost delta estimate for: 12mo vs 24mo term length.

Attaching Soojin's note and the 30-day usage Aaron shared.

Thanks — Ben
Director, Enterprise Sales
[Attachment: nimbus-30d-usage.csv (67KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: Nimbus — capacity and SLO feasibility

Ben —

From a CS/onboarding perspective: Nimbus has a mature infra team and is open to a short pilot to validate the latency profile on Dedicated. If we go the 24mo route we should offer:
- One week of free dedicated capacity for trialing the reserved config (no commitment),
- $30K onboarding credit for ops runbook and playbook creation,
- A success check at 30/60/90 days tied to baseline metrics.

On credits: propose we tier crediting based on term length (12mo: $10K, 24mo: $30K). I'll draft language for the customer-facing playbook.

—Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Gupta <aaron.gupta@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, contracts@nimbus.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: ServiceGuard SLO addendum & pricing — draft

Aaron —

Thanks for your patience. Attached is a concise SLO addendum and a price schedule for both 12- and 24-month commitments. Highlights: 

- 95th percentile latency SLO: <= 200ms for designated low-latency endpoints (we've scoped the endpoints based on your usage export).
- Priority Support Path: Business-hours 1-hour response for Sev-1; 24/7 coverage remains standard for Sev-2/3 with 4-hour and 24-hour targets respectively.
- Capacity: 20% reserved headroom with the option for 2x burst capacity for short windows (billed at reduced burst rate).
- Credits: 24mo gets $30K onboarding credit + one-week pilot of dedicated capacity. 12mo gets $10K credit.

Attachments: service_guard_slo_proposal.pdf (full SLO text) and draft-slo-addendum.docx (redline-ready). Please review and confirm if we should route the final via DocuSign.

Link to draft deal in HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4982
DocuSign room (pre-created): https://www.docusign.com/rooms/xyz-serviceguard-4982

If this looks good, Ben and I can coordinate on term and sign path.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: service_guard_slo_proposal.pdf (94KB)]
[Attachment: draft-slo-addendum.docx (38KB)]

From: Aaron Gupta <aaron.gupta@nimbus.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, contracts@nimbus.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ServiceGuard SLO addendum & pricing — draft

Soojin —

This looks great and exactly in line with what we were hoping for. Two quick asks before we sign: 
1) Can you make the SLO explicitly scoped to the endpoints tagged "low-latency" in our usage export? (we have a small batch of background jobs we don't want included)
2) Please add a 72-hour maintenance blackout window per month (we'll provide preferred windows).

If you can open the DocuSign room for signature and include the 24mo pricing (we'll opt for the 24mo with the $30K credit), we can route internally and sign this week.

Thanks — Aaron
VP Product, Nimbus Analytics
